cards.prose: What Yahusha (Jesus) says Isaiah prophesied is Isaiah's own line, and the picture is the same: the mouth and the lips near, the heart far off. Isaiah goes one step further than Matthew, saying their fear of Yahuah (the LORD) was *taught by the precept of men*, which is the tradition laid over the commandment.
cards.member_phrase: this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's own words, the ones Yahusha (Jesus) says were prophesied of them: lips near, heart far, and a fear of Yahuah (the LORD) taught by the precept of men.

cards.prose: This is the commandment Yahusha (Jesus) sets down in front of them, the fifth of the ten, and it carries a promise of long days in the land. The rule of Corban let a man call his goods a gift and so keep them back from his father and mother, which is how a tradition comes to stand where the commandment stood.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The fifth commandment, the word Corban set aside, with its promise of long days in the land.

cards.prose: Mark carries the same charge and keeps the word Matthew only translates: *It is Corban, that is to say, a gift* (Mark 7:11). In the verse after this one he lets Moses speak the commandment itself, *Honour thy father and thy mother* (Mark 7:10), so the two sides are plain: the word of Elohim (God) on one hand, their own tradition kept at its cost on the other.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Mark's version of the charge, with Corban named and explained as a gift, and the commandment of Elohim (God) set against their own tradition.

cards.prose: Moses tells the people not to add to the word or take anything from it, and the elders had done both at once. A washing rule was piled on top, and the honour owed a father and mother was taken away by Corban. The charge in Matthew is not that they were strict but that they handled the commandment as if it could be changed.
cards.member_phrase: Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it
cards.member_sentence: Moses forbids adding to the commandment or taking from it, the line the tradition of the elders crossed in both directions.

cards.prose: Moses says it a second time, and here it follows his warning not to ask *How did these nations serve their gods?* (Deuteronomy 12:30). Adding to what Yahuah (the LORD) commanded and borrowing someone else's way are set side by side, which is the same fault Yahusha (Jesus) finds in men's commandments taught as if they were doctrine.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The warning against adding to or taking from what Yahuah (the LORD) commanded, given right after a warning against copying another people's ways.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says they teach the commandments of men as if they were doctrine, and Daniel sees the same habit grown to full size, a power that thinks *to change times and laws*. The Pharisees did it with a rule here and a rule there, and the people under that teaching were handed it by those before them.
cards.member_phrase: shall wear out the saints of the El Elyon (most High), and think to change times and laws
cards.member_sentence: A power that thinks to change times and laws: the habit of setting men's commandments where Elohim's (God's) stood, seen full grown.
cards.flag: The old note ties this to the system Daniel sees; I wrote it as the same habit grown larger and did not name a system.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says they teach men's commandments as doctrine, and John gives the plain test for any teaching: whether it stands with his commandments or sets others in their place. The next verse says of the man who claims to know him and does not keep them, *the truth is not in him* (1 John 2:4).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: John's plain test: knowing him is shown by keeping his commandments, not the commandments of men.

cards.prose: The scribes and Pharisees come from Jerusalem with their question, and later in this gospel he names the kind of teaching they speak for: blind guides whose oath rules set the gold above the temple that makes it holy. It is the same ranking Corban made, a gift put above father and mother, and he asks of it, *whether is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift?* (Matthew 23:19)
cards.member_phrase: Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor
cards.member_sentence: The blind guides and their oath rules, which rank the gold above the temple as Corban ranked a gift above father and mother.

cards.prose: The men at the door of this chapter belong to the school Paul came out of, and he says what he was in it: *exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers*. He writes of it without scorn, as a man who stood where they stand and knows from the inside how a tradition passes for the commandment.
cards.member_phrase: being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers
cards.member_sentence: Paul looking back on his own zeal for the traditions of his fathers, the same tradition the scribes bring to Yahusha (Jesus) here.

cards.prose: Paul gives the same warning in his own words, setting what is taught *after the tradition of men* against what is taught after Messiah (Christ). It is the line Isaiah drew and Yahusha (Jesus) repeats here, and Paul puts it beside philosophy and empty deceit, not beside the commandments of Elohim (God).
cards.member_phrase: Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men
cards.member_sentence: Paul's warning against teaching that follows the tradition of men and not the Messiah (Christ), the same line Isaiah and Yahusha (Jesus) draw.

cards.prose: Mark sets the call to the crowd right after the charge that the word of Elohim (God) was made *of none effect through your tradition* (Mark 7:13). So the saying about what defiles grows out of the argument over tradition, and Yahusha (Jesus) turns from the elders to the people to say it, asking every one of them to hear and understand.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Mark's account of the call to the crowd, set directly after the charge that their tradition made the word of Elohim (God) of none effect.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) traces what defiles back to the heart, and Genesis shows that heart long before any washing rule, when *every imagination of the thoughts of his heart* was only evil continually. The mouth only lets out what is already held there, which is why a rinse of the hands cannot reach it.
cards.member_phrase: every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually
cards.member_sentence: The heart's own evil, seen before the flood, is the source the saying points to and no washing of hands touches it.

cards.prose: Jeremiah says of the heart what Matthew says, that the trouble is inside, and then names the one who looks there: *I Yahuah (LORD) search the heart... according to the fruit of his doings* (Jeremiah 17:10). A man is weighed by what his heart brings forth, not by what he ate or whether he rinsed his hands.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The prophet locates the trouble within the heart, where Yahuah (the LORD) searches, and not in what enters the mouth.

cards.prose: If the heart is where defilement starts, Ezekiel promises the answer where it has to be made: Yahuah (the LORD) takes away the stony heart and gives a heart of flesh. He goes on to say what that heart does, *cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them* (Ezekiel 36:27).
cards.member_phrase: I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh
cards.member_sentence: The promise of a new heart that answers the heart Matthew names, a heart that walks in his statutes and keeps his judgments.

cards.prose: Peter was the one who asked Yahusha (Jesus) to explain this saying, *Declare unto us this parable* (Matthew 15:15), and he heard it close on unwashen hands. Years afterward, hungry on a roof, he still answers the voice with *I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean*, so the disciple who heard the saying did not take it to open the food laws.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Peter, who asked for this saying to be explained, still says he has never eaten anything common or unclean.
cards.flag: Acts 10:28 is not in the packet, so I left what the vision meant at what these verses say and did not state it.

cards.prose: A hungry man on a roof and a sheet let down is the scene people hang this saying on. Read in its place, Peter is left asking what it could mean, *doubted in himself what this vision which he had seen should mean* (Acts 10:17), while Matthew's saying never left the subject of bread and *unwashen hands* (Matthew 15:20).
cards.member_phrase: Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour
cards.member_sentence: The vision begins as Peter prays on the housetop and grows hungry, the setting in which Matthew's saying about the mouth must not be read.
cards.flag: Acts 10:28 is not in the packet; I did not say what the vision meant.

cards.prose: The question in Matthew is whether to eat bread with unwashen hands, and the chapter ends on it: *to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man* (Matthew 15:20). What may be eaten is a different subject with its own place, where Yahuah (the LORD) spoke to Moses and Aaron for the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and the saying about the mouth does not reach back and touch it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Where Yahuah (the LORD) begins his word on what may be eaten, a law the saying about unwashen hands leaves standing.

cards.prose: Moses sets the law of what may be eaten inside a word about who the people are, *an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)* (Deuteronomy 14:2), and then says *Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing* (Deuteronomy 14:3). Matthew's saying is about unwashen hands at bread and leaves that law where it stood.
cards.member_phrase: Ye are the children of Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God)
cards.member_sentence: The food law sits among words about who the people are, children of Yahuah (the LORD) and a holy people, and Matthew's saying leaves it standing.

cards.prose: The plant he speaks of is the one in his own parable of the field, where a man sowed good seed and *his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat* (Matthew 13:25). So what the Father has not planted is what the enemy sowed, and the rooting up is the harvest the parable describes.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The parable of the field: good seed sown by the man, tares sown among it by his enemy.

cards.prose: He calls them blind leaders of the blind, and in Matthew 13 he says why such blindness stands: *seeing see not; and hearing they hear not*. To his own hearers he says the opposite, *blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear* (Matthew 13:16), and the leader who cannot see takes those who follow into the ditch with him.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The reason given for those who see and do not see, and hear and do not hear, set against the blessing on those who do.

cards.prose: When the disciples ask to have the parable declared, he says it plainly: *the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one* (Matthew 13:38), and *the enemy that sowed them is the devil* (Matthew 13:39). That is what a plant the Father did not plant means in his own mouth.
cards.member_phrase: his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field
cards.member_sentence: The disciples ask for the parable of the tares, and the answer that follows says plainly whose seed each plant is.
cards.flag: I did not name the Pharisees as the tares; the parable speaks of what was sown, and the text of Matthew 15 does not make that identification.

cards.prose: If every plant the Father did not plant is rooted up, Isaiah says what is left standing: *the branch of my planting, the work of my hands*. The rooting up is for the sake of the planting, a people all righteous who inherit the land for ever.
cards.member_phrase: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah names what the Father did plant: his people, the branch of his planting, who inherit the land for ever.

cards.prose: He calls them blind leaders here and blind guides there, and in Matthew 23 he says what the guiding was: an oath rule that counted the gold above the temple that makes it holy, so that *the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold* (Matthew 23:17) was turned upside down. It is the system's rule he names, and the people led by it are the ones in danger of the ditch.
cards.member_phrase: Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor
cards.member_sentence: The blind guides named again, with the oath rule that shows what their guiding put first.
cards.flag: The old note only says 'blind-guides language'; I used the oath rule to show what the guiding was.

cards.prose: On the coast of Tyre and Sidon a woman will call out to him, and at Capernaum a centurion has already come, *beseeching him* (Matthew 8:5). Both are far from the assembly in the land and both come asking for someone at home, and both are sheep of the scattered house who heard the Shepherd where they were.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The centurion who came to him at Capernaum, one of the scattered house found under Rome, as the woman is on the coast.
cards.flag: The existing thread's title and summary read the woman as a stranger who joined herself by faith; that is the opposite of the brief and the thread text needs rewriting.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) goes out of the land to the coast of Tyre and Sidon, and Ruth begins with a man of Beth-lehem-judah who had gone out of it the same way, *to sojourn in the country of Moab*. His sons took wives of Moab, and Ruth became one with the line by marrying Boaz. That is the marriage road, and it is not the woman's, who is already one of the sheep.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: A family of Beth-lehem-judah living in Moab, where Ruth, a woman of Moab, was taken as a wife and came into the line by marriage.
cards.flag: Old note made Ruth a precedent for the woman; I kept her as the contrasting case, since Ruth came in by marriage and the woman is seed already.

cards.prose: The word of Yahuah (the LORD) sends Elijah to *Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon* (1 Kings 17:9), the same coast Yahusha (Jesus) enters here. A widow there had already been commanded to sustain him, so the word had reached her before the prophet did, and she was one of his sheep in the place she had been scattered to.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The word of Yahuah (the LORD) that sent Elijah to a widow of Zidon, on the same coast Yahusha (Jesus) enters.

cards.prose: Naaman is a Syrian commander in a land set against Yashar'el (Israel), yet the Syrians had *brought away captive out of the land of Yashar'el (Israel) a little maid* (2 Kings 5:2), and it is her word that sends him to the prophet. Like the woman on this coast, he is found in the place of the scattering, reached through a daughter of the house.
cards.member_phrase: Now Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honourable
cards.member_sentence: Naaman, a Syrian commander in the land of the scattering, reached by the word of a captive girl of Yashar'el (Israel) in his own house.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) names this coast himself at Nazareth: of all the widows in Elijah's day, *unto none of them was Elijah sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon* (Luke 4:26), and the one leper cleansed was Naaman the Syrian. The synagogue was *filled with wrath* (Luke 4:28), and now he stands on that same coast.
cards.member_phrase: many widows were in Yashar'el (Israel) in the days of Elijah, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months
cards.member_sentence: His own words at Nazareth naming the widow of Sidon and Naaman, the two places the prophets reached beyond the land.

cards.prose: Hebrews honors Rahab's faith, *perished not*, as Yahusha (Jesus) honors this woman's, *great is thy faith*. They are not the same road, though. Rahab was spared at Jericho and then became one with the line by marrying Salmon, a man of Yahudah (Judah), while the woman on this coast is a sheep he was sent to, and he never says she became anything.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Rahab's faith honored, a case of its own, since she came into the line afterward by marriage.
cards.flag: The old note says this is the same thing the woman shows; I kept the faith in common but separated the two ways in, since Rahab came by marriage.

cards.prose: What he says to the woman he had already said of the centurion, *so great faith, no, not in Yashar'el (Israel)*, and he goes on to say that many will *sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven* (Matthew 8:11). Both are sheep of the scattered house who heard him from afar, and the faith shows it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: His marvel at the centurion's faith, said of a man found outside the assembly in the land, the same praise he gives the woman.

cards.prose: She answers with *Truth*, taking the order of the house as it is, and still asks for what falls from the table. The centurion did the same, *I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof* (Matthew 8:8), and he marvelled at both. Neither argues the order, and both ask from inside it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The centurion's lowly asking and the faith Yahusha (Jesus) marvelled at, answering the woman's own low asking at the table.

cards.prose: She does not ask to be seated at the table, only for what falls from it, and she agrees the children come first. Ruth's road to that house began where Ruth begins, with a family of Beth-lehem-judah in Moab and a woman of Moab taken as a wife, and it ended with her made one with Boaz by marriage. The woman at Tyre comes by no such door, but as a sheep.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Ruth's way into a house of Yahudah (Judah) was marriage, a different door from the woman's at the table.
cards.flag: Kept the old note's Ruth connection as a contrast; the brief says never to mix Ruth with the woman of Canaan.

cards.prose: When he says he is sent to the lost sheep, this is the Shepherd of Ezekiel speaking: *will both search my sheep, and seek them out*. His seeking reaches into *all places where they have been scattered* (Ezekiel 34:12), and here it reaches a coast far from the land.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The Shepherd's own promise to search for and seek out his scattered sheep, which he is doing on this coast.

cards.prose: Jeremiah gives the lost sheep their history: *their shepherds have caused them to go astray*, and they have *forgotten their restingplace*. Yahusha (Jesus) names them as the ones he is sent to, and the verses before show what their coming back looks like, *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall come, they and the children of Yahudah (Judah) together* (Jeremiah 50:4).
cards.member_phrase: My people hath been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray
cards.member_sentence: The lost sheep named by the prophet, led astray by their shepherds, whose return brings both houses together.

cards.prose: Before he says it to the woman he had said it to the twelve: not the way of the Gentiles and not into a Samaritan city, but *go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Matthew 10:6). It is one boundary, so when he tells her he is sent only to those sheep, he is not making a new rule, and her answer shows she was inside it.
cards.member_phrase: Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not
cards.member_sentence: The boundary he gave the twelve is the one he repeats to the woman, the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) first.

cards.prose: Paul says it of Yahusha (Jesus) in his own words: he was *a minister of the circumcision* so as *to confirm the promises made unto the fathers*. That is the same boundary as *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)*, a sending to the people the promises were given to, and the promises are confirmed, not replaced.
cards.member_phrase: Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of Elohim (God), to confirm the promises made unto the fathers
cards.member_sentence: Paul restates the mission as a sending to the people of the promises, to confirm what Elohim (God) promised the fathers.

cards.prose: Before the cross he says he is sent only to *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)*, and after it the disciples are sent to teach *all nations*. The sending widens in place and not in people, for the sheep were scattered into every nation and the word has to go where they are.
cards.member_phrase: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations
cards.member_sentence: The sending after the cross goes out to every nation, the places the lost sheep were scattered to, and not to a new kind of people.
cards.flag: The old note's point kept: the commission widens by territory of the dispersion, not to the nations as a covenant category.

cards.prose: The sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) are scattered, and the woman of Canaan is one of them, called by the name of the coast she was scattered to. What Paul calls *the fulness of the Gentiles* is those same sheep found in every place they were driven and gathered home, not strangers added to the house.
cards.member_phrase: blindness in part is happened to Yashar'el (Israel), until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in
cards.member_sentence: Blindness in part to Yashar'el (Israel) until the fulness of the Gentiles comes in, the lost sheep found in every place they were scattered.

cards.prose: John sent to ask *Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?* (Matthew 11:3), and Yahusha (Jesus) answered with what could be seen and heard. On the mountain by the sea of Galilee the crowd sees those same works for itself and gives its own answer, glorifying the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.member_phrase: The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear
cards.member_sentence: The works he told John to report, the blind seeing and the lame walking, done again in front of the multitude.

cards.prose: The hands and the pattern are the same as at the first feeding, but the numbers change: seven loaves here and *seven baskets full* (Matthew 15:37), five loaves there and *twelve baskets full* (Matthew 14:20). And this time he gives his reason in his own words, *I will not send them away fasting* (Matthew 15:32).
cards.member_phrase: he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude
cards.member_sentence: The first feeding with the same acts, he took, blessed, broke, and gave through the disciples, with five loaves and twelve baskets over.

cards.prose: These are the same acts that fed the crowd in the wilderness, done now at the table on the night he is betrayed, with words said over the bread. The meal also looks ahead, *until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom* (Matthew 26:29).
cards.member_phrase: Yahusha (Jesus) took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples
cards.member_sentence: The same taking, blessing, breaking and giving at the last supper, where he says what the bread is and looks to his Father's kingdom.

new_threads.title: The plant my heavenly Father hath not planted, and the blind leaders
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. The Father has always had a planting, and the older scriptures already knew the difference between what he planted and what was sown over it. When his disciples tell him the Pharisees were offended, Yahusha (Jesus) says:

*But he answered and said, Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.* (Matthew 15:13)

The plant he means is the one in his own parable of the field, where one man sowed and an enemy sowed after him.

*Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:* (Matthew 13:24)

*But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.* (Matthew 13:25)

When the disciples ask for the parable to be declared, he does not leave it a riddle.

*The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one;* (Matthew 13:38)

So a plant the Father did not plant is what the enemy sowed, and what is rooted up is judged at the harvest and not by us. Isaiah says what remains standing when it is done.

*Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.* (Isaiah 60:21)

The next words in Matthew turn from the plants to the guides who lead people among them.

*Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch.* (Matthew 15:14)

He had already said why such blindness stands.

*Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.* (Matthew 13:13)

And later he shows what the guiding looked like, in the oath rule that put the gold first.

*Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!* (Matthew 23:16)

It is the system and its rule that he names. The ones who follow it are the people in danger of the ditch, and that is why he speaks of them as he does.
